title: Add representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline v12
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: consolidate representative workload runners and profiling baselines into a single, repeatable reporting pipeline (v12) to improve stability of performance baselines and make nightly profiling runs resilient to infra noise. This PR introduces: 1) new representative workload runners for chat, completion, and embedding scenarios with configurable sequence-length distributions and user-behavior sampling; 2) profiling baseline artifacts (trace configs, kernel-level metrics, and a small baseline dataset) so we have deterministic inputs for perf regression checks; 3) a reporting pipeline that aggregates runner outputs, normalizes metrics, produces per-model baselines, and uploads reports to the internal metrics store and S3; 4) CI and workflow updates to schedule nightly and on-demand runs; 5) small infra/helm tweaks so benchmark lab can scale horizontally and isolate heavy profiling runs. Summary of changes: - benchmark-lab/runners: add new runner modules (chat_runner.py, completion_runner.py, embeddings_runner.py) with sampling profiles and synthetic prefix generator - benchmark-lab/profiling: add baseline manifests, synthetic datasets, and trace collectors - benchmark-lab/reports: implement reporting pipeline v12 (normalization, regression detection, report uploader) - perf-canary: add job definition for scheduled nightly profiling runs - observability-pack: add dashboards and alert rules for benchmark regressions - ci/workflows: add scheduled workflow and on-demand dispatch; update runner test matrix Checklist: - [x] Add representative workload runners - [x] Add profiling baselines and trace configs - [x] Add reporting pipeline and uploader - [x] Update CI workflows and infra templates - [x] Add docs for running locally and interpreting reports Testing and validation: Ran the reporting pipeline end-to-end against the local mini-cluster and against ci-staging. Nightly job executed successfully in ci-staging for three consecutive runs; metrics aggregator deduplicated and normalized latency and p50/p95/p99 values. Observability dashboards display baselines and a simple regression alert correctly triggered in a synthetic test. Backwards compatibility: existing benchmark job names and artifact schemas are preserved; new fields are optional. Rollout plan: merge to main, deploy benchmark-lab service chart to staging, enable nightly profiling for a week, monitor alerts and false positive rate, then rollout to prod. Notes: this PR purposefully keeps runner configurations small (no huge synthetic corpora) and wires into the existing upload and report schema to avoid downstream churn.
